topology_reasoning.device_identification: The target is a compact grating-assisted directional coupler / contra-directional coupling section. It has two broad upper/lower slab or bus regions facing each other across a narrow central interaction region. The function-defining feature is a set of long, narrow, parallel horizontal material bars/teeth running across the interaction region, with matching tooth stacks etched into the inner faces of the upper and lower regions. Curved/thick side transitions at left and right connect the broad regions to external waveguides or slabs.
topology_reasoning.operating_principle: The repeated parallel bars form a periodic perturbation in the coupling gap between two optical paths. Coupling strength and spectral response are governed mainly by bar pitch, bar duty/thickness, guide/slab width, gap between the opposing regions, and the effective interaction length. The side transitions set access/taper loss and preserve the two-port topology.
topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Use only gdsfactory rectangles and gf.Path extrusions. The central grating bars are rectangles. The upper/lower slabs are thick extruded horizontal paths with rounded joins, plus etched-looking white gaps approximated by drawing the visible material teeth as individual rectangles/paths rather than a filled raw polygon. Side transitions are represented by tapered/curved gf.Path extrusions. No raw polygons or device stencils are used.
